title: IG Metall workers hold warning strike and rally in Ingolstadt

tea.why: Workers are seeking higher wages and job security during ongoing collective bargaining for the metal and electrical industry.
tea.want: A five percent wage increase, 110 euros more in training compensation, and secure employment.
tea.changed: Nov 9: The third round of collective bargaining in Munich concluded without an agreement.

summary: On November 9, 2026, members of the IG Metall union held a large-scale warning strike and rally in Ingolstadt, Bavaria, as part of a broader series of industrial actions across the state. Employees from Audi, Airbus Manching, and other regional companies gathered at the Audi-Piazza to support their demands for a five percent pay raise, increased training allowances, and job security. The union reported that approximately 110 companies across Bavaria were involved in the day's actions. While the union estimated 15,000 participants in Ingolstadt, local police reported 8,000 attendees. The protest coincided with the third round of tariff negotiations in Munich, which ended without a resolution. Employers criticized the strikes and expressed concerns regarding job losses in the sector, while union leadership emphasized the workforce's readiness for further action.
response: The employers' association vbm criticized the warning strikes and stated that no progress could be achieved with the union during the third round of negotiations. They also highlighted the loss of 11,000 jobs in the industry this year.

crowd.text: The union estimated 15,000 participants, while police reported 8,000.

updates.text: IG Metall held a major warning strike and rally in Ingolstadt alongside other cities in Bavaria.
The third round of collective bargaining between IG Metall and the vbm employer association concluded in Munich without an agreement.
